strengths: The paper introduces a novel, feed-forward, zero-shot 3D style transfer method using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) that operates on unposed, multi-view images, eliminating the need for slow per-scene optimization or precomputed camera poses.

The proposed architecture elegantly decouples geometry and style by extracting geometric attributes purely through the self-attention pathway of a shared backbone, while style is injected via global cross-attention to predict color/spherical harmonic coefficients.

The introduction of the voxel-based 3D style loss is a strong technical contribution. Voxelizing the features before computing statistics ensures style consistency in 3D space, which successfully mitigates multi-view inconsistencies inherent in 2D-based losses.

Comprehensive experimental results show that Stylos outperforms strong optimization-based baselines (such as StyleRF and StyleGS) both quantitatively (in short-range and long-range view consistency metrics) and qualitatively.
weaknesses: Comparison with concurrent feed-forward methods, such as Styl3R, is missing (though the authors note its code was not available). Comparing against a naive baseline, like a feed-forward reconstruction model (e.g., AnySplat) combined with a 2D frame-by-frame stylization, would have further highlighted the value of the proposed 3D style loss and unified network design.

The performance is highly bound to the reconstruction capability of the underlying geometric backbone (VGGT/AnySplat). If the feed-forward reconstruction fails or yields low-quality geometry under challenging viewpoints, the quality of the style transfer degrades as a result.

The computational and memory overhead of the voxel-based style loss during training is not explicitly discussed. Since the loss involves unprojecting and voxelizing high-dimensional VGG feature maps, a discussion on how much this slows down Stage 2 fine-tuning compared to standard 2D style losses would be beneficial.

As shown in Section 4.1, the visual quality of the model degrades when the number of views per batch exceeds 32, representing a scalability bottleneck that warrants further discussion or potential mitigation strategies.

strengths: Eliminates the need for costly per-scene optimization and precomputed camera poses, performing 3D stylization in a single forward pass directly on unposed multi-view inputs.

Introduces an innovative voxel-based 3D style loss that unprojects and aggregates multi-view features into a 3D voxel grid to match style statistics, effectively enforcing view-consistency and geometry-aware stylization.

The decoupled architecture design—with a dedicated Style Aggregator utilizing global cross-attention and a separate geometric backbone with self-attention—effectively preserves structural integrity while transferring complex styles.

Demonstrates strong quantitative and qualitative performance over existing state-of-the-art baselines (StyleRF, StyleGS) on standard datasets, showing superior cross-view consistency (LPIPS/RMSE) and style expression (ArtScore).
Excellent writing quality and reproducibility, accompanied by highly detailed pseudocode for the loss formulations and extensive additional qualitative results in the appendix.
weaknesses: There is a visible trade-off between style intensity and geometric structure. As shown in the qualitative comparisons, Stylos can sometimes produce slightly 'washed out' or conservative stylization compared to optimization-based methods, which over-impose style patterns at the cost of geometry.

Scalability is somewhat limited by the number of views per batch; as discussed in Section 4.1, performance degrades when the batch size exceeds 32 views, indicating susceptibility to unstable Gaussian representations on larger view sets.

The paper lacks a comprehensive analysis of the voxelization resolution in the 3D style loss, leaving it unclear how grid resolution choices impact overall memory overhead, runtime, and the granularity of style transfer.

The framework relies heavily on the pretrained backbones and pipelines of VGGT and AnySplat, meaning the architectural novelty is somewhat incremental and bounded by the performance of these base models.

strengths: Addresses a highly challenging and practical setting: feed-forward 3D style transfer of unposed multi-view content (or even single images) without requiring per-scene optimization or precomputed camera poses.
Proposes a novel 3D voxel-space style loss that aligns aggregated 3D features with 2D style statistics, which mathematically enforces 3D style consistency over traditional 2D image-level losses.

Employs an elegant dual-pathway architecture where geometry prediction is kept clean with self-attention, and style is injected using global cross-attention, avoiding style representations from corrupting the underlying geometry.
Provides extensive qualitative results in the appendix and includes detailed pseudo-codes for the proposed losses to aid reproducibility.
weaknesses: The model exhibits performance degradation when scaling to larger view counts (e.g., more than 32 views), causing edge artifacts and lower visual quality. This limits the scalability of the framework in large, complex scenes.

The approach is heavily dependent on the performance of the underlying VGGT/AnySplat reconstruction backbone. Any failures or errors in the feed-forward camera pose and depth predictions directly cascade into artifacts in the stylized output.

The quantitative evaluation is relatively limited, focusing on only four scenes from the Tanks and Temples dataset. Testing on a broader range of scenes/datasets or conducting a user study would make the performance claims more robust.
Minor typos are present in the manuscript, such as 'imamge' instead of 'image' in the captions of Figure 8 and Figure 14.

strengths: The paper proposes a novel single-forward framework (Stylos) for 3D Gaussian Splatting stylization that does not require per-scene optimization or precomputed poses, making it highly practical and efficient.

A novel voxel-based 3D style loss is introduced to align aggregated scene features with 2D style statistics in 3D voxel space, effectively enhancing cross-view consistency and geometry-aware stylization.
The design of the shared-backbone with dual pathways (geometry reasoning and style injection) is well-thought-out, ensuring that style features do not distort the underlying geometric structure.

Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments on benchmarks like CO3D and Tanks & Temples show superior style consistency, artistic quality, and inference speed compared to recent state-of-the-art baselines.
The paper includes solid ablation studies, helpful qualitative failure cases in the appendix, and controllable style interpolation experiments.
weaknesses: The framework relies heavily on the VGGT backbone, meaning its performance is bounded by the quality of the 3D reconstruction. As noted in the limitations, cluttered scenes with high-frequency structures or large numbers of input views tend to degrade the reconstruction and, consequently, the stylization.
The Style Aggregator replicates a deep Transformer architecture (24 layers, matching the backbone) which significantly increases the overall model size and parameter count.
The voxelization process relies on a fixed discretization grid (voxel size of 0.002), which could act as a bottleneck for high-resolution rendering or fine-detailed style patterns.

strengths: Eliminates per-scene optimization: Unlike most prior 3DGS or NeRF stylization techniques, Stylos is a feedforward model that does not require expensive optimization or precomputed camera poses, enabling 3D style transfer in just 0.05 seconds.

Innovative voxel-level style loss: The introduction of a 3D voxel-based AdaIN style loss effectively bridges the gap between 2D style statistics and 3D geometric consistency, significantly reducing cross-view texture flickering and inconsistency.

Decoupled architecture: The dual-pathway Transformer design carefully isolates geometric reconstruction from style injection, ensuring that structural geometry remains stable and faithful while allowing global style features to be effectively integrated.

Excellent quantitative and qualitative results: Stylos consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple challenging benchmarks (CO3D, Tanks & Temples, DL3DV) in both visual quality and short/long-range consistency metrics.
Thorough and transparent appendix: The authors provide detailed implementation specifications, comprehensive ablation studies, scaling analysis, and an honest showcase of failure cases.
weaknesses: Resolution limitations: Due to the constraints of feedforward processing on unposed multi-view inputs, Stylos is evaluated at lower preset resolutions (e.g., 448x448) compared to optimization-based methods which can process full-resolution images.

Tight coupling with backbone performance: The quality of the final stylized output heavily relies on the robustness of the underlying geometry backbone (VGGT). Errors in estimated depth or camera poses translate directly to visual artifacts in the stylization.

Scaling challenges with high view counts: As analyzed in Section 4.1 and Figure 4, when the number of input views scales up significantly (e.g., above 32 views), the visual quality exhibits a gradual decrease, introducing edge artifacts on complex structures.

strengths: Unposed feed-forward pipeline: Unlike most existing 3D stylization methods that require costly per-scene optimization and precomputed camera poses (SfM), Stylos performs zero-shot feed-forward 3DGS stylization directly from unposed multi-view or single images.

Novel 3D Voxel-based Style Loss: The proposed 3D voxel style loss addresses the visual inconsistency of standard 2D-based style losses by aggregating features in a 3D voxel grid before computing AdaIN statistics.

Strong Efficiency: Eliminating per-scene optimization results in a massive speedup (0.05 seconds vs. several minutes or hours for optimization-based methods), making real-time interactive stylization feasible.

Comprehensive Evaluation: The paper provides a thorough quantitative and qualitative evaluation across multiple benchmarks (CO3D, Tanks & Temples, DL3DV-10K) and includes extensive ablation studies of key architectural and loss components.
weaknesses: Incremental Architectural Novelty: The framework relies heavily on pre-existing building blocks (VGGT for unposed camera estimation, DINOv2 for feature representation, and AnySplat for feed-forward Gaussian prediction). The main architectural changes (introducing cross-attention style pathways) are relatively straightforward and highly dependent on the robustness of these underlying backbones.

Degradation in Stylization Quality (Blurriness/Fidelity): Compared to optimization-based methods (e.g., G-Style, StylizedGS, SGSST), the feed-forward predictions of Stylos often suffer from blurry textures and lower stylistic fidelity (as seen in Figure 5 and the additional results). The stylization sometimes resembles global color-shifting rather than high-fidelity artistic stroke transfer.

Geometric Artifacts and Sensitivity: Since geometry is predicted in a feed-forward manner, inaccuracies in the VGGT/AnySplat backbone (e.g., due to cluttered scenes, thin structures, or varying numbers of input views) directly degrade the quality of the stylization. This limitation is visible in the failure cases shown in Figure 11.

High Memory Overhead & Scaling Issues: The 3D voxelization and cross-view global attention scale poorly with the number of input views. As analyzed in Section 4.1 and Figure 7, both runtime and peak memory increase significantly when the batch size exceeds 16–32 views, and visual quality degrades at larger view counts (e.g., 64 views in Figure 4).
